---
title: Typed Keys
description: How i18next-cli generates types for t(), and the current wiring status in v1.
---

## Purpose

Typed keys make `t('common.actions.save')` a compile error when the key does not exist. The package
generates the supporting types with `i18next-cli types` from the catalog JSON.

## Generated Files

| File | Generated by | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/i18n/src/@types/resources.d.ts` | `i18next-cli types` | default-exports a `Resources` interface mirroring every catalog key |
| `packages/i18n/src/@types/i18next.d.ts` | `i18next-cli types` | augments i18next's `CustomTypeOptions` |

`i18next.d.ts` looks like this:

```ts
// This file is automatically generated by i18next-cli, because it was not existing.
// You can edit it based on your needs: https://www.i18next.com/overview/typescript#custom-type-options
import type Resources from './resources';

declare module 'i18next' {
  interface CustomTypeOptions {
    enableSelector: false;
    defaultNS: 'common';
  }
}
```

## Regenerating

```bash
pnpm i18n:extract
pnpm i18n:types
```

Run extraction first so the catalogs are current, then types. Commit both the catalogs and the two
generated files together.

## How It Is Intended to Work

`resources.d.ts` describes the exact key tree, and i18next's TypeScript integration reads it through
`CustomTypeOptions.resources`. Once wired, a bogus key becomes a type error and editor autocomplete
suggests real keys.

## Current State in v1

The generated `i18next.d.ts` imports `Resources` and sets `defaultNS: 'common'` and
`enableSelector: false`, but it does **not** yet merge `Resources` into `CustomTypeOptions.resources`.
That wiring is a recorded deferral, so in v1 `t()` is typed by i18next's defaults rather than by your
catalog. You can opt in locally by adding the `resources` field to `CustomTypeOptions` in your own
project's declaration file.

## Behavior and Edge Cases

- `defaultNS: 'common'` means a bare `t('actions.save')` is looked up in `common`; other namespaces
  require `t('ns:key')` or the `useT('ns')` hook form.
- `keySeparator` is `.` and `nsSeparator` is `:`, so the fully qualified form is
  `<namespace>:<segment>.<segment>`.
- `removeUnusedKeys: false` means extraction does not delete keys, so the resources type can contain
  keys no longer in use.
